editorial:
Imagine a world where every kid has a high-tech robot best friend that tracks their every move and helps them find friends online. You meet Barney, a lonely 11-year-old who just wants to fit in, but his new bot, Ron, is a total disaster. Unlike the other robots that come pre-programmed with fake personalities, Ron is a blank slate who doesn't know how to behave. This creates a hilarious and sweet dynamic because while other kids have perfect digital buddies, Barney has to actually teach Ron how to be a friend. It feels like a modern take on a classic buddy comedy, blending a bright, colorful world with a story about real human connection.

What really works here is the pacing and the funny way Ron learns about the world. The animation is clean, and the chemistry between the two main characters feels genuine. One small downside is that the plot gets a bit predictable toward the end, but the heart of the story makes up for it. You should definitely watch this with your family on a rainy weekend. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV for those crisp colors. Or, if you love owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move.
endingExplained: In the end, you see that the company behind the bots is using them to spy on kids and control their friendships. Barney and Ron team up to expose the CEO and shut down the system. They prove that real friendship is about hard work and loyalty, not an algorithm. The movie wraps up with the kids learning to talk to each other in person again, while Ron remains a unique, glitchy friend who is loved for being different.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about friendship and funny robots.
